ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: The sex determination mode of goats is XY type. The pedigree chart as shown indicates the inheritance of a certain trait in goats; the dark color in the figure indicates individuals showing this trait. It is known that this trait is controlled by a pair of allelic genes. Under the condition of not considering chromosomal variation and gene mutation, answer the question: Based on the pedigree chart, is this trait inferred to be a recessive trait or a dominant trait?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The sex determination mode of goats is XY type. The pedigree chart as shown indicates the inheritance of a certain trait in goats; the dark color in the figure indicates individuals showing this trait. It is known that this trait is controlled by a pair of allelic genes. Under the condition of not considering chromosomal variation and gene mutation, answer the question: Based on the pedigree chart, is this trait inferred to be a recessive trait or a dominant trait?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the pedigree chart, dark symbols indicate individuals showing this trait. Ⅱ-1 is an unaffected male white square, and Ⅱ-2 is an unaffected female white circle; among their offspring, Ⅲ-1 is a dark male square showing this trait. Then reason: The question states that this trait is controlled by a pair of allelic genes, and chromosomal variation and gene mutation are not considered. If this trait is a dominant trait, then an offspring showing this trait generally must obtain a dominant expression gene from one of the parents; under the condition of no mutation, two unaffected parents should not give birth to offspring showing the phenotype. In the figure there appears the phenomenon of "appearing out of nothing" in which two unaffected parents give birth to an affected individual, which conforms to the rule that recessive traits are shown in phenotypic offspring born from carrier parents. Therefore, it is inferred that this trait is a recessive trait.
